title: 간판 속 한자어 읽기: 한 글자씩 나누면 뜻이 보여요
objective: By the end, you can split a Sino-Korean word on a sign or notice into its syllables and use them to find what a place is, what is not allowed, and what you pay for.
summary: Learners use the meaning of common Sino-Korean syllables to guess new words on signs, building guides and notices.
note: You do not need to read Chinese characters. Just learn what each Korean syllable means.

task.title: Guess words from syllables
task.line: Split each word into syllables, use the meanings you learned, and then answer.

sections.heading: Key syllables you see every day

items.text: It means going in, as in 입구 (entrance).
It means going out, as in 출구 (exit).
It names a way in or out, as in 비상구 (emergency exit).
At the end of a word, it names a room, as in 회의실 (meeting room).
At the end of a word, it is often a large place, as in 주차장 (parking lot).
It names a small place for one job, as in 매표소 (ticket office).
At the end of a word, it names a store, as in 편의점 or 서점.
It is money you pay for something, as in 입장료 (entrance fee).
It means something is forbidden, as in 금연 (no smoking).
It is about eating, as in 식당 and 식사.

sections.heading: Word order inside the word
paragraphs: In many Sino-Korean words, the action comes first and the thing comes second, like in English: 등산 = climb + mountain, 독서 = read + book. Native Korean puts the thing first (산에 올라가요). If the first syllable is an action like 입, 출 or 금, read the word as 'enter/exit/forbid + something'. The last syllable often tells you what kind of thing it is (실, 장, 소, 점, 료).

sections.heading: Watch out: same sound, different meaning
paragraphs: One Korean syllable can come from different Chinese characters. 장 in 주차장 means 'place', but 장 in 반장 (class leader) and 회장 (chairperson) means 'head, leader'. If the word is a person, think 'leader'. If it is somewhere you go, think 'place'.

exercises: The last syllable tells you what kind of thing it is. Is it a room, a place or a fee? ① 대기실 ② 수영장 ③ 사용료
Choose the right word for the situation: ① You are leaving Korea at the airport. (입국 / 출국) ② A country buys cars from abroad. (수입 / 수출)
Fill in the blank with 금, 점 or 실: ① 여기서 사진 촬영은 ___지예요. ② 이 빵은 역 앞 제과___에서 샀어요. ③ 진료___ 앞에서 이름을 부를 때까지 기다려 주세요.
Read the notice and answer Yes or No. [박물관 안내] 입장료: 무료 · 음식물 반입 금지 · 물품 보관소: 1층 ① 들어갈 때 돈을 내야 해요. ② 안에서 빵을 먹어도 돼요. ③ 가방은 1층에 맡길 수 있어요.
Does 장 mean 'place' or 'head (leader)' here? ① 시장에서 과일을 샀어요. ② 우리 회사 사장님은 아주 친절하세요. ③ 삼촌은 자동차 공장에서 일해요.
answers: ① a room (waiting room) ② a place (swimming pool) ③ a fee (usage fee)
① 금 (금지) ② 점 (제과점) ③ 실 (진료실)
① No (무료 = free) ② No (음식물 반입 금지 = no food allowed inside) ③ Yes (물품 보관소 = storage for your things)
① place (시장 = market) ② head (사장 = company head) ③ place (공장 = factory)
